title: Markets Try to Rebound as Asia Rushes Rescue Measures
description:
Wall Street futures jump after the worst weekly drop in 19 months. S&P 500 tests key support while commodities unwind, Bitcoin battles $61K, and Nvidia faces new regulatory scrutiny.

Sources: Jeremy Lefebvre Clips, Michael Pizzino, MindTheChart

segments.heading: Futures Rebound After Crash
segments.narration: Wall Street futures are jumping nearly 2% after the worst weekly drop in nineteen months. Global markets are scrambling to stabilize after a violent tech sell-off pushed major indices into correction. Today we break down the broad commodity crash, critical equity support levels, and new scrutiny facing Nvidia.

segments.heading: Wall Street Snapshot
segments.narration: Market volatility remains high after last week's deep technical correction. The S&P 500 closed down 3.7% at 6,910, extending its five-day drop to 8.6%. The Nasdaq Composite fell 5.3% to 22,618, bringing its weekly loss to 10.0%. The Dow Jones dropped 1.9% to 48,147. European benchmark equities also slid, with the FTSE MIB falling 2.5% to 48,704 and the Euro Stoxx 50 dropping 2.8% to 5,942. The VIX volatility index surged 26.2% to 35.9, reflecting sharp hedging activity across equity options. U.S. 10-year Treasury yields eased to 4.91%. Crude oil sits near $83.58 per barrel. Stock futures are rebounding this morning, but structural overhead pressure remains heavy across global equity markets.

segments.heading: Commodity Market Drawdown
segments.narration: Major asset classes are experiencing a broad liquidity unwind following months of elevated valuations. Commodity weakness is expanding well beyond energy into industrial and precious metals. Silver dropped 21.5% over the past month, while copper futures fell nearly 14% on weakening global manufacturing demand. WTI Crude oil has declined 21% month to date, keeping energy pressure subdued. Gold trades near $3,608 per ounce despite a 2.7% daily bounce, remaining down over 6% across five trading sessions. Excessive portfolio leverage and aggressive risk-taking have exacerbated drawdowns across these volatile markets. When commodities and equities decline together, capital shifts rapidly toward cash and short-duration paper. Lower commodity prices may keep medium-term inflation manageable, but immediate downside risk persists until buyer volume returns to key structural support floors.
bullets: Crude oil declines 21% month to date

segments.heading: S&P 500 Technical Levels
segments.narration: Equity indices remain vulnerable despite Sunday evening's futures pop. The equal-weight S&P 500 has recorded seven consecutive red weeks, a structural breakdown seen only twice before over the last quarter century, in 2002 and 2022. The U.S. Dollar Index has pushed above 103.8, absorbing strong safe-haven flows while global equities face steady liquidation. For the S&P 500 to establish a meaningful market bottom, it must reclaim and consolidate above the 7,250 to 7,350 resistance zone. Without consolidation above former breakdown levels, any short-term rally risks creating another lower high on monthly technical charts. The Nasdaq faces similar structural resistance near its 28,000 yearly start level. Until these key overhead zones are broken, broader technical trends favor defensive positioning.

segments.heading: Bitcoin Bear Market Cycle
segments.narration: Crypto assets are attempting to find structural support following severe liquidations across major tokens. Bitcoin trades near $61,035, up 1.6% on the day, while Ethereum holds around $1,723. Bitcoin recently snapped a 17-day losing streak after touching lower support near $55,000. Interestingly, the current crypto bear market has reached 411 days, matching historical market cycles down to the exact timeframe. However, long-term technical indicators remain suppressed across multi-year charts. Bitcoin continues to trade far below its 200-day exponential moving average near $77,097. Price stability requires reclaiming and maintaining key resistance at $67,000. If Bitcoin fails to defend its current base, lower support sits near $60,000, delaying potential multi-month recovery targets into early 2027.

segments.heading: Nvidia Scrutiny & Rescue
segments.narration: Fresh regulatory and geopolitical headlines are impacting technology sector sentiment. Government officials are seeking clarification on Nvidia chip sales to China following tighter export enforcement rules. In addition, an unconfirmed report has surfaced regarding past executive contacts with foreign intelligence agencies, adding headlines to chipmakers. Meanwhile, emergency interventions are underway across Asian financial hubs. Authorities in China, South Korea, and Taiwan have introduced stock market rescue measures ahead of Monday trading to curb panic selling. Nvidia stock dropped 14% last week, driving broader semiconductor weakness. Whether Asian liquidity measures can stabilize global tech equities depends on corporate buyback execution and earnings resilience in coming quarters.
bullets: U.S. examines Nvidia China chip sales

segments.heading: Macro Data This Week
segments.narration: Economic catalysts will steer market sentiment during this Thanksgiving-shortened trading week. On Monday at 03:15 Eastern Time, France releases flash manufacturing and services PMI figures, followed by German PMI data at 03:30 Eastern Time. United States flash manufacturing PMI lands Monday at 09:45 Eastern Time, with forecasts at 54.5. On Tuesday at 10:00 Eastern Time, the Conference Board reports Consumer Confidence data. Wednesday features major economic prints at 08:30 Eastern Time: preliminary third-quarter GDP is forecasted at 3.5%, Core PCE price index month-over-month is expected at 0.3%, and weekly unemployment claims are projected at 201,000.
bullets: U.S. Flash PMI Monday at 09:45 ET
Core PCE and GDP Wednesday at 08:30 ET

segments.heading: Congressional Trading ETF
segments.narration: An unusual exchange-traded fund tracks political stock transactions by replicating disclosures filed by Democratic members of Congress. While the ETF allows retail investors to copy legislative moves, public filings arrive with weeks of delay. Coupled with higher management fees, the fund often struggles to track fast market turns during deep technical corrections.
bullets: Delayed filings lag rapid market shifts

segments.heading: Final Thoughts
segments.narration: This briefing is for informational purposes only and is not financial advice. Stay disciplined during high volatility. Follow for tomorrow's update.
